c.tagline: Thuringia's medieval capital, where an inhabited bridge crosses the Gera and Luther studied.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; you can hail on the street, wait at a rank, or book by phone or app. Ride-hailing apps FreeNow, Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police. Both are free and staffed by English-speaking operators.

hood_desc: One of Germany's largest and best-preserved medieval old towns, threaded by the Gera river and centred on the Fischmarkt; home to the Kraemerbruecke — Europe's longest inhabited bridge, still lined with shops and houses — plus the Mariendom and St. Severi churches on their hill; best for first-timers who want the historic core on foot.

The old craftsmen's quarter northwest of the centre, a warren of narrow lanes and half-timbered houses that survived the war, now dotted with small hotels, wine bars and workshops; atmospheric, quiet and central, popular with those wanting old-Erfurt charm.

A leafy 19th-century district south of the old town toward the Steigerwald forest, with villas, the Egapark gardens nearby and easy tram links; a calm, green residential base within reach of the sights.

A quiet residential quarter southwest of the centre near the Theater Erfurt, the Bruehler Garten and the Augustinian riverside, with parks and local eateries; suits travellers wanting a relaxed, less touristy stay close to the old town.

Erfurt's grand central boulevard and main shopping and transport hub, lined with Wilhelmine department stores, the Angermuseum and cafes, and the meeting point of most tram lines; a convenient, lively base right at the city's crossroads.

water.note: Tap water is high quality and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30am to around 11:30pm, with a Nightliner network on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: No tap-in gates: buy tickets in the EVAG app, at machines, or from the driver, and validate before boarding; one ticket covers EVAG trams and buses across the VMT network. A single ride is about €2.30 (~$2.50) and a day ticket about €5.90. Staying weeks? The €58/month Deutschland-Ticket covers local transit nationwide.

bus: Erfurt ZOB (Central Bus Station, at the Hauptbahnhof)

transit.m: Tram line 4 to city centre / Anger (~15 min, every 10-15 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals round the bill up to the next euro or add about 5-10% for good service, handed to the server rather than left on the table.

landmarks: Krämerbrücke (Merchants' Bridge)
Europe's longest inhabited bridge north of the Alps, a medieval crossing lined end-to-end with half-timbered shops, galleries and chocolatiers.
Erfurt Cathedral (Dom St. Marien)
A soaring Gothic cathedral atop a monumental staircase, home to the Gloriosa, one of the world's largest free-swinging medieval bells.
Severikirche (Church of St. Severus)
The five-naved early-Gothic church standing shoulder-to-shoulder with the cathedral, together forming Germany's most striking twin-church silhouette.
Petersberg Citadel
One of Europe's best-preserved baroque town fortresses, its star-shaped bastions and underground passages overlooking Erfurt's spire-studded skyline.
Augustinian Monastery (Augustinerkloster)
The austere Gothic monastery where Martin Luther lived as a monk from 1505 to 1511, its cloisters and Luther cell still intact.
Old Synagogue (Alte Synagoge)
One of Europe's oldest surviving synagogues, dating to the 11th century and UNESCO-listed, displaying the astonishing medieval Erfurt Treasure hoard.
Fischmarkt and the Rathaus
The old town's showpiece square, ringed by Renaissance patrician houses and the neo-Gothic town hall with its romantic historical murals.
Domplatz
One of Germany's largest medieval market squares, spread beneath the cathedral steps and transformed each December into a famously atmospheric Christmas market.
Anger Square
Erfurt's elegant main boulevard-square, lined with gorgeously restored Gründerzeit facades, fountains and the Angermuseum's art collections.
Egapark
A sprawling horticultural park on the Cyriaksburg fortress grounds, famous for Europe's largest ornamental flowerbed and its panoramic observation tower.

train.note: Erfurt Hauptbahnhof is a ten-minute walk south of the Anger and the cathedral square, with trams outside the door. It was rebuilt as the crossing point of the Berlin-Munich and Frankfurt-Dresden high-speed lines, which makes it one of the best-connected medium-sized cities in Germany: Berlin and Munich are both around 2h, Frankfurt about 2h and Leipzig 45 minutes. No train crosses a border from Erfurt - change at Nuremberg or Munich for Austria and Italy, at Frankfurt for France and the Benelux, and at Dresden for Prague. Regional services are operated by DB Regio and Erfurter Bahn across the Thuringian network.

bus.note: Erfurt has no scheduled international coach. FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) is the main long-distance operator, using the stops at the Hauptbahnhof with services to Berlin, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Nuremberg and Munich, from where the European network connects. Tickets are online only in practice, and journey times are Berlin about 4h, Frankfurt 3h30 and Munich 5h - generally slower than the train, so the coach is a price play rather than a time saver.

ferry.note: Erfurt sits on the small river Gera in landlocked Thuringia with no navigable waterway, so there are no ferries or scheduled passenger boats of any kind.

half.name: Weimar
half.blurb: Former home of Goethe and Schiller, a short hop east with Bauhaus sites and the Duchess Anna Amalia Library.

half.name: Eisenach & Wartburg Castle
half.blurb: Hilltop medieval castle where Martin Luther translated the New Testament while hiding under an assumed identity.

half.name: Jena
half.blurb: University town in a river valley known for its Zeiss optics heritage and the striking JenTower skyscraper.
